tei:titleStmt.tei:title: עֵת שַׁעֲרֵי אַרְמוֹן – תפילה לאסתר המלכה
‘Et Sha'are Armon – Prayer of Queen Esther, a piyyuṭ for Purim by the Diwan Ashira Project

tei:div.tei:head: ‘Et Sha'are Armon – Prayer of Queen Esther, a piyyuṭ for Purim by the Diwan Ashira Project

tei:lg.tei:l: While the palace enclosures engulf me,
One by one the fences encircling my heart give way.
Warned of veiling Your face on the day of admonition,
The altar itself sheds tears of my suffering!
Ejected from my mother’s womb,
An orphan without father or any consolation,
I am, facing my mockers, desperate
As a sheep surrounded by seventy wolves.
While my people lie, feverish, in exile.
The altar itself sheds tears of my suffering!
Then came the time that the stupid king in Susa
Enthroned me to replace his queen,
Ignorant of my origins.
I would not have closed my eyes if He who does not sleep,
King Supreme, had withdrawn His protection.
The altar itself sheds tears of my suffering!
The enemy cast lots for the extermination of the singular people
And Mordechai let out a cry of terror. He told me:
“Cousin, now has come the time to act to save the tribes of Israel!
If your star must lose its light,
Act relentless, that no world may exist where the moon ceases to shine!”
The altar itself sheds tears of my suffering!
Heavenly angels, tell my mother
That the apple of her eye is consumed by fire.
Tell my Father to cry hot tears,
Tell the Father of orphans that the sun does not disappear.
The warmth of their embrace sorely absent.
The altar itself sheds tears of my suffering!
Sons and daughter of my people — Jews of Susa
Come together and fast for me.
If my flesh must be trampled like the earth,
May you salvation grow from it – me, I die:
In this feverish body beats a serene heart!
The altar itself sheds tears of my suffering!
May He who brought justice to Dinah come to my rescue
And show the imprisoned bird the way out.
May He keep my soul safe;
May His word oppose all evil.
Let the myrtle branch (Hadas) never wither!
The altar itself sheds tears of my suffering!
Inscribe my remembrance in the annals,
Observe the festivals until the twilight of generations.
Because a day of mourning and wrath was overturned
To become a day of light, of gladness, of rejoicing and of song
In which the rose of Israel will blossom;
The altar dries, at last, its tears!
